_about: Reviewer and translator context. Read by tests and tools/i18n-review-pack.mjs; never bundled. `prefixes` describes groups of keys by their longest matching prefix; `keys` adds a note for one key; `limits` is the widest a string may be, counting a CJK character as 2 and anything else as 1, because the control it sits in has a fixed size.

Used in several places: buttons, group labels and flock counts.
Loading screen, shown while the field is prepared. Short status lines that replace each other.
Title screen, standing directly on the painted grass.
Title screen row showing the player's random running name, which is what appears on the leaderboard.
Shown during play. The aria-style labels are read by screen readers and are not visible.
Panel shown when every sheep is in the pen.
Quiet keyboard reminder at the bottom of the screen during play on a computer.
Round buttons on a touch screen, used with a thumb during play. *Label strings are read by screen readers only.
Recovery dialog after the graphics driver stops the game.
Options in the Render quality select in Settings.
Options in the Follow camera turning select in Settings.
One line under the Follow camera turning select, describing the selected option.
Volume slider labels in Settings. These are sound groups: meadow ambience, sheep, the dog, field objects such as the gate, and interface clicks.
Rows that rebind a key in Settings.
Customization screen, called the Studio: a panel beside a live 3D preview of the dog and flock.
Camera angle buttons in the Studio's dog preview. Small buttons in one row.
Dog coat options in the Studio. A name with a one-line description.
Flock mix options in the Studio. A name with a one-line description.
Sheep breed details in the Studio's sheep registry. Names are real British breeds and places, which are proper nouns. Keep the Latin spelling or use the established local spelling.
One sheep's card in the Studio's sheep registry.
Sheep registry in the Studio: search, filters and a grid of numbered sheep.
Solo leaderboard panel. A run is one game from start to the last sheep penned.
The player's own history inside the leaderboard panel.
Screen reader label for the online results area.
Share button and the sentence sent with a shared link.
Status messages from the online score service. Playing never depends on it.
Labels floating over dogs and pens in multiplayer.
Multiplayer dialog: rooms for 2 to 4 players. Co-op shares one pen. Competitive shares one flock with a pen for each player.
Error shown when a room request fails.
Why a match stopped. Fits inside 'Match interrupted: ...' and 'Interrupted: ...'.
One small line under the Play button, shown once to a player whose browser is in this language. Written in this language, naming this language. They can ignore it and play.

keys.common.sheepCount.one: Singular form. Some languages use the same text for both forms.
keys.common.runTimer: A stopwatch for the current run.
keys.boot.preparing: Small caps line under the game's name. The game has exactly one field.
keys.boot.step.shaders: Cel shading is the game's painted look.
keys.title.kicker: Tagline, rendered in capitals where the script has them. The goal of the game in five words.
keys.identity.runningAs: {name} is a player name such as Mossy Lamb. A running name, as in a race.
keys.hud.sprint: Tiny label above the stamina bar, in capitals.
keys.hud.gate: Screen reader label for a small compass that points to the gate of the pen.
keys.pause.kicker: Quiet line above Paused. Poetic rather than literal.
keys.done.kicker: Quiet line above the finishing time.
keys.done.title: Button returning to the title screen. Means the screen, not a title of a work.
keys.format.ordinal: A rank such as 12th. Use {n} for the number. English alone uses {ordinal}, which already carries its suffix. It also stands alone on a run row in a narrow column, so keep it short: a sentence that needs a word such as 'place' carries that word itself.
keys.scores.rank: {rank} is a plain number, not format.ordinal, so add whatever the language needs around it: 12위, 12位, 第12名.
keys.done.weekRank: {rank} is format.ordinal. {players} is a bare count of players. Name the noun if the count would otherwise read with the next word: in Indonesian and Malay, '340 minggu ini' says 340 weeks. The same goes for done.allTimeRank, share.weekRank and share.historyRank.
keys.times.thatWeek: Stands in for {week} in times.captionOtherWeek when no date is known, so it must read correctly in that sentence.
keys.touch.sprint: Fits a 76 px circle. Hold to run faster.
keys.touch.bark: Fits a 92 px circle. The dog barks at nearby sheep. A verb or short noun.
keys.touch.camera: Fits a 72 px circle. Switches the camera view.
keys.settings.language: Row label for the language picker. Each language's name appears in its own script.
keys.settings.languageUnreviewed: Shown under the language picker in a language no native speaker has checked. Say plainly that it has not been reviewed.
keys.settings.languageReport: Link to the project's public issue list.
keys.settings.legal: {licence} is AGPL-3.0-or-later. Do not translate that identifier.
keys.settings.source: Link to the source code. This notice is a licence requirement.
keys.settings.marker: An accessibility option: a blue ring under the dog for colour-blind players.
keys.studio.title: As in an artist's studio.
keys.studio.roll: A short button that picks a random name, as in rolling dice.
keys.studio.dogIntro: A working collie is a dog that really herds sheep, not a pet breed term.
keys.title.moreFrom: Small heading above links to the studio's other sites on the title screen, and the name a screen reader gives those links. Instrukt Labs is a name: keep it in Latin. The site names themselves are not translated.
keys.angle.hero: A three-quarter view from the front, the flattering angle.
keys.registry.scopeLabel: Label before three small flock size buttons. Keep it short.
keys.registry.search: Placeholder in a small search box. # means the sheep's number.
keys.registry.nameRemainingTitle: The ledger is the game's fixed list of sheep names.
keys.times.weekOf: {date} is a day and month, the Monday the week starts on.
keys.times.captionOtherWeek: {week} is the 'week of' phrase with a date in it, or times.thatWeek while none is known. A word that contracts with what follows cannot go before it.
keys.scores.emptyOtherWeek: {week} is the 'week of' phrase with a date in it.
keys.share.historyRank: {week} is the 'week of' phrase with a date in it.
keys.share.title: {clock} is a time such as 1:23.4.
keys.player.label: {number} is 1 to 4.
keys.mp.winner: {players} is one name such as Player 2. Singular verb.
keys.mp.winnerForfeit: {players} is one name such as Player 2. A forfeit means the others left.
keys.mp.winnersShared: {players} is a list such as Player 1 and Player 2. Plural verb.
keys.mp.winnersSharedForfeit: {players} is a list such as Player 1 and Player 2.
keys.mp.listJoin: Joins two player names. Keep the spaces your language needs at the start and end.
keys.mp.result.one: Singular form for one sheep. {seconds} is a number such as 83.4.
keys.mp.pillReady: Small status pill beside a player.
keys.mp.pillWaiting: Small status pill beside a player.
keys.mp.pillReconnecting: Small status pill beside a player.
keys.mp.incompatible: The player's game is out of date compared with the server.
keys.mp.reason.other: Fallback for a reason this version of the game does not know.
keys.mp.notice.other: Fallback for an error this version of the game does not know.
keys.stats.outcome.forfeit_win: A win because the other players left.
keys.offer.prompt: A short question. English never shows this; translate it as an offer to play in your own language.
keys.offer.accept: A one-word answer on a small button.
keys.offer.decline: A short answer on a small button. It is remembered, and the offer does not return.
